newsitem.title: CHINA: China city shuts Japan golf jv after tax evasion.
newsitem.headline: China city shuts Japan golf jv after tax evasion.

text.p: Tax authorities in China's Shenzhen city have shut a Sino-Japanese joint venture golf club and frozen its assets after the owners failed to pay taxes and fines, the Shenzhen tax bureau said in a statement on Thursday.

Officials in the southern city aim to auction off the Honichi Golf Leisure Club Co's operating rights on the two-million-square meter (22 million sq feet) golf course and its facilities unless the club pays taxes and fines, the statement said.

The club had to start paying taxes and fines amounting to about 120 million yuan ($14.5 million) within 15 days from Wednesday, said the statement, which was carried in the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily newspaper.

"Since the club was set up, it has not submitted any tax for its membership income according to the law ... our bureau has decided to seal up and freeze its assets starting on July 9," the tax bureau said.

The dispute stems from the refusal of the Japanese partner, whose name newspapers gave in Chinese as the Anle Development Co, to remit membership income to Honichi, leaving the joint venture without funds for tax payment, official media has said.
Representatives of the Japanese side have been quoted as saying there was no need to pay tax to China under the Sino-Japanese Double-Taxation Prevention Treaty.
Earlier this year, the tax bureau seized 14 million yuan from Honichi's bank accounts and auctioned the club's 10 cars for about five million yuan, the newspaper said.

The Shenzhen Bao Heng (Group) Co Ltd, the club's Chinese partner, has asked the China International Economic and Foreign trade Arbitiration Commission to end the relationship with the Japanese partner, official media has said.
